I have written Python in 12 public repositories, from 2015 to 2026; in 7 of them it is the main language.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (4), [Media and art](@/projects/media.md) (3), [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (2) and [Knowledge](@/projects/knowledge.md) (1).

Most recently: [Kompendium](@/work/kompendium-epistemicke-anihilace.md): A book, a website and a wiki: mechanisms, detection signatures, defence and recovery, cross-linked into a graph you can explore; [openttd-prismatic-bridge](@/work/openttd-prismatic-bridge.md): REST/Swagger bridge onto OpenTTD's Admin Network, for prismatic-platform; [Sonic Playground](@/work/sonic-playground.md): A hand-picked music blog built with Phoenix and Elixir on the Kita theme.

7 of these projects run as live sites.

I also used it in client work under confidentiality agreements. Roles: Architect, Lead engineer, AI engineer, Data engineer, Investigator and Advisor. What was solved: LLM agents, Decision support, AI transformation, Audit trail and OSINT investigation. The use cases below give the principle and the intent of that work; no client, person, date or number is named.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Python: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Python to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
